options.text: How long the page takes to finish loading
How quickly the page visually responds to interactions like clicks, taps, and key presses
The size of the JavaScript bundle

questions.explanation: INP (Interaction to Next Paint) is the responsiveness vital: it measures the latency from an interaction to the next visual update, reporting near the worst interaction of the visit.

questions.prompt: Match each part of an interaction's latency to a fix that targets it.

pairs.right: Break up long tasks and yield to the main thread
Do less in the handler; defer non-urgent work
Shrink the DOM and make rendering cheaper

questions.explanation: Input delay is fixed by keeping the main thread free, processing time by doing less work, and presentation delay by making the next frame cheaper to render.

questions.prompt: Main-thread work that runs for more than 50 ms and blocks the page from responding is called a ____ task.
questions.explanation: A long task exceeds 50 ms on the main thread. Because JavaScript is single-threaded there, a long task blocks input until it finishes — the main cause of input delay.

questions.prompt: Which techniques help reduce INP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Break up long tasks and yield to the main thread
Update the visible UI first, then defer analytics/logging
Do all work synchronously inside the event handler

questions.explanation: Breaking up tasks, deferring non-urgent work, and debouncing all keep interactions cheap. Doing everything synchronously in the handler inflates processing time and delays the response.

questions.prompt: Inside an event handler, which work should run synchronously?

options.text: Only the visible response the user is waiting for; defer the rest
All analytics and logging first, then the UI update
Every possible task, to get it out of the way

questions.explanation: Do just the visible response synchronously so the user sees a fast reaction, then yield and run non-urgent work (analytics, logging) after the browser paints.

questions.prompt: Order a responsive click handler that avoids blocking the interaction.

items.text: Show immediate visual feedback (e.g. a spinner)
Yield so the browser can paint that feedback
Do the heavy work in yielding chunks

questions.explanation: Give feedback first, let the browser paint it, then do heavy work in chunks that yield, and finally run non-urgent work — so the interaction never blocks.
